lines.text: A chest X-ray model trained at one hospital, deployed at another. Accuracy drops. Confidence doesn't.
Ninety-nine point nine percent confident. On an adult film, from a model trained only on children.
It can't warn you. A softmax has two outputs. There's no third that says, I don't recognise this.
ScanProof runs four checks on every prediction. Typicality. Stability. Agreement. Confidence. Then pass, review, or block.
Here's why one number isn't enough. This film is normal, at ninety percent confidence.
Change the gamma. A windowing difference no radiologist would report. The model flips. Five of twenty-one perturbations change the label.
Now the real failure. Trained on children in Guangzhou. Run on adults at the N I H.
Confidence goes from ninety-three point six to eighty-six. It barely moves. On breast ultrasound it climbs back up.
Typicality goes from the fiftieth percentile to the ninety-eighth. The pass rate falls from sixty-two percent to four point eight.
Just resolution? A control arm runs the pediatric films through the adult set's exact resampling path. One point. It's the population, not the pixels.
Confidence is the best in-distribution error ranker. Embedding distance is the best shift detector. Neither is good at both, and we publish where ours loses.
Different failures trip different wires. Here, typicality caught it alone. On the fragile film, stability did.
Thresholds frozen before the test split was scored. Public benchmark data. Ninety tests, thirty-two preflight checks.
ScanProof. Four checks. One decision. And the evidence behind it.
